channel.title: Deseret News - Faith
channel.description: Faith news and stories from Deseret News

item.title: Religious schools fight for their identity
item.description:
St. Dominic Academy, a Catholic school in Auburn, Maine, and its diocese petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court on Nov. 20 to review Maine rules that require private schools taking public tuition money to follow state nondiscrimination laws on religion, sexual orientation and gender identity. The court has not decided whether to take the case, which could help define how far states can condition public funding as the justices weigh a similar Colorado preschool dispute.

In July, the First Circuit sided with the school only on a rule affecting religious expression, upholding Maine's limits on religious preference in admissions and its gender identity protections. Becket attorney Ben Fleshman said St. Dominic seeks "narrow exemptions" to sustain a Catholic community, while Maine says it has a compelling interest in keeping public money from funding discrimination against students.


Sources:

  • Religious schools fight for their identity - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Mariya Manzhos

item.title: Feel and express gratitude for missionary work, Elder Gilbert tells missionaries
item.description:
Elder Clark G. Gilbert of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said his mission was where he first came to know that Jesus Christ can help people through whatever they face. The apostle, who served 37 years ago, has felt grateful for his mission every day since, Church News reports.

Elder Gilbert said Jesus can help people find "peace, hope, healing and happiness".


Sources:

  • Feel and express gratitude for missionary work, Elder Gilbert tells missionaries - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Church News

item.title: Screwtape goes to college
item.description:
Max McLean's Fellowship for Performing Arts is touring college campuses with a stage version of C.S. Lewis' The Screwtape Letters, and VanDenBerghe writes that the shows are drawing full houses and letting students take up deep spiritual questions. McLean and his cast say themes from the 1942 book, from traditional morality to the role of suffering, feel as relevant as ever, or more so, to today's students.

FPA campus initiative manager Whitney Bahr said some students "cry in recognition" during performances, and McLean, who holds a Q&A after every show, said students are "hungry to explore questions of the soul".


Sources:

  • Screwtape goes to college - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Betsy VanDenBerghe

item.title: Church of Jesus Christ leaders share Thanksgiving messages
item.description:
Five apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints posted Thanksgiving messages on Thursday, following church President Dallin H. Oaks' Thanksgiving Eve invitation to thank God for adversities. Their posts ranged from scripture and testimony to Elder Bednar's attempt to count his blessings in 60 seconds and the Japanese phrase for gratitude Elder Gilbert shared with missionaries in Provo.

President Christofferson cautioned that ingratitude can be "deadening" and tied to entitlement, while President Uchtdorf said gratitude "helps you remember that sorrow is not the whole story".


Sources:

  • Church of Jesus Christ leaders share Thanksgiving messages - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Ariel Harmer

item.title: Before BYU beat Kansas, these staff members shared messages of faith
item.description:
Two BYU football staff members, mental performance director Braden Brown and assistant safeties coach Danny Sorensen, told a packed BYU Athletics fireside in Kansas City how football led them to trust God, the day before BYU beat Kansas 31-29 in triple overtime. Elder Clark G. Gilbert of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles spoke first, reminding the more than 100 fans that they would also represent the church at the game.

Brown, who became a therapist after a back injury ended his NFL career, told fans, "You don't have to feel confident to keep moving forward". Sorensen, who won a Super Bowl with the Chiefs, added that "our Heavenly Father sees the whole field".


Sources:

  • Before BYU beat Kansas, these staff members shared messages of faith - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Krysyan Edler

item.title: Art can help people feel the Spirit as they visit the temple, President Uchtdorf says
item.description:
Speaking Nov. 19 at the Utah State Capitol, President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles' acting president, said every child of God is able to create and can invite the Spirit through those creations. His remarks came at the Inspirational Art Association's 16th annual Christmas Season Art Showcase, and the full Church News report is on TheChurchNews.com.

He described the urge to create as a "yearning", saying "we each have an inherent wish and desire to create something that did not exist before".


Sources:

  • Art can help people feel the Spirit as they visit the temple, President Uchtdorf says - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Church News

item.title: Church of Jesus Christ leader teaches why giving thanks is essential for growth
item.description:
In a social media post the day before Thanksgiving, President Dallin H. Oaks of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints urged people to give thanks even for their hardships and trials. He invited people to thank God for their adversities and seek guidance in meeting them, teaching that each person came to earth to be tested and to face opposition.

Giving thanks in all things, President Oaks wrote, lets people "see hardships and adversities in the context of the purpose of life". The post echoes his April 2003 general conference address, "Give Thanks in All Things".


Sources:

  • Church of Jesus Christ leader teaches why giving thanks is essential for growth - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: Here’s when Temple Square fully reopens for Christmas season
item.description:
Temple Square in Salt Lake City is fully open to holiday visitors for the first time in seven years, now that the construction that reshaped the campus is complete. Its Christmas lights switch on Friday at 4:30 p.m. and stay on nightly through New Year's Day, with decorations reaching closer to the Salt Lake Temple than ever before.

Jay Warnick, Temple Square's manager of ground services, said the redesign was meant to improve the visitor experience as well as the grounds' beauty: "Much was put into accessibility and flow". New this season is a light tunnel of cards hung by people worldwide sharing their feelings about Jesus Christ, and the historic cedar of Lebanon tree will be lit for the first time since construction began.


Sources:

  • Here’s when Temple Square fully reopens for Christmas season - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Dan Rascon

item.title: Federal judge had an observation after hearing in Latter-day Saint trademark case against podcaster
item.description:
U.S. District Judge Robert Shelby heard arguments Tuesday in Salt Lake City on podcaster John Dehlin's bid to dismiss the trademark suit The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints brought against him and his company, Open Stories, and hinted the two sides should look again at settling. His written ruling on the motion could be weeks or months away.

Church attorney David Jordan repeated that the church would settle without any change to the Mormon Stories name if Dehlin added a spoken disclaimer that the show isn't church-affiliated, saying it is the mix of logos, colors and fonts that the church believes "willfully creates confusion". Shelby said the day's discussion made him wonder whether the parties are "as far apart as they thought they were six months ago."


Sources:

  • Federal judge had an observation after hearing in Latter-day Saint trademark case against podcaster - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Tad Walch

item.title: Episode 324: Sharing peace and providing relief through Giving Machine kiosks
item.description:
The latest Church News podcast, recorded on location after the global launch of the Light the World Giving Machines, has reporter Mary Richards interviewing leaders of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and of nonprofit groups about the kiosks and the deeper reason for Christmas giving. The machines are now in 145 cities across 28 countries, their widest reach yet.

Elder Peter M. Johnson, a General Authority Seventy, called Jesus "the ultimate giver and the Prince of Peace" during the launch remarks.

  • Episode 324: Sharing peace and providing relief through Giving Machine kiosks - deseret.com

item.title: What Africa’s Christian boom means for the world
item.description:
A new Pew Research Center report projects that sub-Saharan Africa will become the center of global Christianity in coming decades, home to nearly 54% of the world's Christians, Mariya Manzhos writes in the State of Faith newsletter. Baylor University historian Philip Jenkins told Manzhos that African churches are already shaping worship in Europe and the U.S. and influencing debates over same-sex relationships and women's leadership.

"There have never been a billion Christians on any continent before", Jenkins said. The newsletter also notes that U.S. Catholic bishops voted to advance the sainthood cause of Maria Middleton, a Pennsylvania 18-year-old who died of a brain tumor in 2020 and could become the first Gen Z saint.


Sources:

  • What Africa’s Christian boom means for the world - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Mariya Manzhos

item.title: New song ‘Seek Peace’ teaches children how to share the Savior’s peace
item.description:
A new song for children in the Hymns for Home and Church collection, titled Seek Peace, aims to show young members how they can share the Savior's peace. Church News places the song alongside the focus on peacemaking from church President Dallin H. Oaks and the late President Russell M. Nelson.

"I urge you to choose to be a peacemaker, now and always," President Nelson said in an April 2023 general conference talk.


Sources:

  • New song ‘Seek Peace’ teaches children how to share the Savior’s peace - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Church News

item.title: First Latter-day Saint temple in this Pacific Island nation nears completion
item.description:
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints will dedicate its Port Moresby Papua New Guinea Temple on April 25, 2027, making it the first operating temple of the faith in that Pacific nation. Free public tours are planned from March 17 to April 3, excluding Sundays.

Membership there has grown from more than 28,000 when the temple was announced in 2019 to about 46,000, and many members have traveled to distant temples such as the one in Suva, Fiji. Local member Pelyne Keket wanted the temple built "so we can go back inside," she said in a social media video posted soon after the 2019 announcement.


Sources:

  • First Latter-day Saint temple in this Pacific Island nation nears completion - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: Salt Lake Temple rededication scheduled for late 2027
item.description:
The First Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints announced Monday that the renovated Salt Lake Temple will be rededicated on Dec. 5, 2027, eight years after it closed. The date comes about two months after a six-month public open house ends, leaving time to clean and repair wear from the tours.

Steel and tension cables now bind the towers, walls and foundation together atop a base isolation system that lets the temple withstand earthquakes up to magnitude 7.3. In its announcement, the First Presidency said it rejoices "in the completion of the work on this historic and sacred edifice" now that the remodel is finished.


Sources:

  • Salt Lake Temple rededication scheduled for late 2027 - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Tad Walch

item.title: Church of Jesus Christ leaders dedicate new temples in California, Mexico
item.description:
Apostles Quentin L. Cook and Gary E. Stevenson dedicated the Modesto California and Torreón Mexico temples on Sunday, the 230th and 231st temples of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The Modesto dedication gives California 10 dedicated temples, second among U.S. states only to Utah.

Elder Cook called the temple "a place of thanksgiving, refuge, instruction and understanding" in a difficult world. "They have almost in their DNA this idea of connecting to ancestors," Elder Stevenson said of Mexican culture, and organizers said 24,314 people toured the Torreón temple during its open house.


Sources:

  • Church of Jesus Christ leaders dedicate new temples in California, Mexico - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Mary Richards and Joel Randall

item.title: Elder Cook dedicates Modesto California Temple, ‘a place of thanksgiving’
item.description:
Elder Quentin L. Cook, a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, led the Sunday, Nov. 22, dedication of the Modesto California Temple, calling it a place of thanksgiving as the holiday week began. He said the Latter-day Saint temple comes "with numerous blessings" for God's children.


Sources:

  • Elder Cook dedicates Modesto California Temple, ‘a place of thanksgiving’ - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Church News

item.title: 10 years in, here’s how Giving Machine donations are reaching millions
item.description:
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints' Light the World Giving Machines have brought in $70 million for charities since the first appeared in 2017, and leaders of participating nonprofits say the donations have widened their reach. Days for Girls International, for example, reached 48,000 more girls and women in the past year through the machines.

The church covers all operating costs, and charities may spend no more than 10% of funds on overhead. African Girls Hope Foundation founder Grace Nkundabantu, who once could not afford school herself, said the machines let her group "help more girls every single year" since joining four years ago.


Sources:

  • 10 years in, here’s how Giving Machine donations are reaching millions - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: Faithfully and joyfully preparing for the Modesto California Temple dedication
item.description:
Shannon Hawkins, who coordinated the Modesto California Temple's open house and dedication with her husband, Matthew, said guests encountered motifs such as almond blossoms as soon as they reached the welcome desk, but were reminded that the focus inside is on Jesus Christ, whose large picture hangs right behind it. Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles is set to dedicate the temple on Sunday, Nov. 22.

item.title: How ‘The Heart of America’ became the heart of the Giving Machines movement
item.description:
Kansas City has emerged as a hub of the Giving Machines movement, raising more than $1.3 million for charities since they arrived in 2021, thanks in large part to Chiefs coach Andy Reid and Tammy Reid, who made the machines a family holiday tradition, and Tammy Reid has recruited stars like Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce and Paul Rudd to film promotional videos. She hosted the 2026 launch at Union Station on Friday for a fifth year with Tavia Hunt, and Elder Clark G. Gilbert of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles announced church food donations for the area. Cynthia McDavitt, who served five years as city lead and whose communication council's 15-page pitch helped bring the machines to Kansas City, said, "Tammy knows everybody, so she would just call up Paul Rudd and ask him to do a video."


Sources:

  • How ‘The Heart of America’ became the heart of the Giving Machines movement - deseret.com

item.title: More Salt Lake Temple open house tickets coming soon
item.description:
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints will release a fourth batch of Salt Lake Temple open house tickets on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 11 a.m. MST, following heavy demand for earlier releases that saw the first 1 million tickets claimed in under a day. Running from April 5 to Oct. 1, 2027, under the theme "Rejoice in Christ", the open house will give the public its first look inside the temple in 134 years, and a virtual tour and other online experiences will be offered for those who can't travel to Salt Lake City. The tours are about "coming closer to Jesus Christ", Primary General President Rosemary K. Chibota told a September press event.


Sources:

  • More Salt Lake Temple open house tickets coming soon - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: ‘You are one tough sucker’: Steve Young learned he had separation anxiety in an NFL training room
item.description:
Steve Young was the NFL's reigning MVP in 1993 when anxiety nearly drove him from the season, Tad Walch writes in a ChurchBeat newsletter excerpt, and his turning point came after a win over Atlanta, when he confided in 49ers team doctor James Klint, who told him he'd had separation anxiety as a child and that it was normal. Speaking to 10,000 students at BYU-Idaho in Rexburg on Tuesday, Young, who went on to therapy, said a fresh wave over the past year was "unlike anything I have experienced in my adult life." He now tells college students to reject constant worrying as one more of the bargains he once struck with his anxiety, saying Christ's invitation to fear not is "not asking us to be braver" but a call out of a transactional pattern.


Sources:

  • ‘You are one tough sucker’: Steve Young learned he had separation anxiety in an NFL training room - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Tad Walch

item.title: ‘Be not afraid,’ President Uchtdorf teaches at Utah Valley Institute devotional
item.description:
Speaking in Orem on Nov. 15, President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, acting president of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, drew six lessons from the Old Testament king Jehoshaphat for Utah Valley Institute of Religion listeners facing fear, worry or difficult choices. Uchtdorf warned against reading the account as a guarantee that faith makes every trial vanish, saying "Some battles are long." The complete Church News report is available at TheChurchNews.com.


Sources:

  • ‘Be not afraid,’ President Uchtdorf teaches at Utah Valley Institute devotional - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Church News

item.title: 3 new exhibits chronicle the Salt Lake Temple’s history and influence
item.description:
Ahead of the Salt Lake Temple's first open house for the public since 1893, the downtown Church History Museum in Salt Lake City has opened three exhibits that will stay up through the Salt Lake Temple Celebration, which runs April 5 to Oct. 1, 2027. Fitly Framed Together follows the temple from construction to dedication through lesser-known contributors such as Antonio Scappatura, a Catholic stonemason from Sicily who may have cut a temple stone on display; All Nations Shall Flow Unto It gathers depictions of the temple from abroad, including a Peruvian textile and batiks from Sierra Leone and Indonesia; and One by One: Gathered unto Christ tells 55 conversion stories, among them that of Hare Teimana, a Māori chief baptized in 1882. Museum director Riley Lorimer said the hope is that visitors will be "inspired by stories that they may not have heard before" and see people of every background strengthening the church.


Sources:

  • 3 new exhibits chronicle the Salt Lake Temple’s history and influence - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: Which religion will be the world’s largest in 2035? Pew offers a projection
item.description:
A new 300-page Pew Research Center report projects that Muslims will overtake Christians as the world's largest religious group by 2035 and number about 3.6 billion to Christians' 3 billion by 2070, with lead author Conrad Hackett calling natural population increase the biggest factor, well ahead of religious switching. Pew's Alan Cooperman said the shift isn't a contest between the faiths, since most growth for each will come where it already predominates, and the report expects Congo to pass the United States as home to the most Christians by 2070, 299 million to 174 million. In the U.S., Christians are projected to slip from 62% of the population to under half by 2070 while still being the largest group, as the unaffiliated grow from 28% to 41%.


Sources:

  • Which religion will be the world’s largest in 2035? Pew offers a projection - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Mariya Manzhos and Jacob Hess

item.title: Man sentenced to decades in prison for child sex abuse crimes in Ohio and Utah
item.description:
U.S. District Judge Edmund Sargus on Tuesday sentenced Wade Christofferson, 73, to 45 years in federal prison after he pleaded guilty to coercing and enticing a Utah girl under 10, to whose home he had mailed coded, sexually explicit letters from Ohio for about six months. The U.S. Attorney's Office said investigators confirmed about 20 instances of hands-on abuse of victims in Utah and Ohio, and Sargus, who said a life term wouldn't be consistent with other cases, called the sentence essentially a life sentence. U.S. Attorney Dominick S. Gerace II said the evidence showed a sexual interest in children that "spanned decades"; the defendant's older brother is President D. Todd Christofferson, second counselor in the Latter-day Saint First Presidency.


Sources:

  • Man sentenced to decades in prison for child sex abuse crimes in Ohio and Utah - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Tad Walch

item.title: Fear fueled Steve Young. A new bout of anxiety reveals fresh insight for following Christ
item.description:
At a BYU-Idaho devotional in Rexburg on Tuesday, former 49ers quarterback Steve Young, 65, said the separation anxiety he believed he had outgrown came back over the past year harder than anything he had felt as an adult, and that facing it showed him fear had been the deepest bargain of his life all along. Young told the 10,107 students that believing enough worry can control outcomes is "magical thinking," the same transactional mindset he has long preached against, and that Christ's repeated command not to fear invites people out of that pattern rather than asking them to be braver. He urged them to keep caring while dropping the belief that their anxiety earns God's help, saying trust "is where love leads".


Sources:

  • Fear fueled Steve Young. A new bout of anxiety reveals fresh insight for following Christ - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Tad Walch

item.title: Light the World turns 10 with a record number of Giving Machines
item.description:
Last year's Giving Machine donations paid for 3.5 million meals and vaccinated 500,000 children, and this season the red machines from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, where shoppers buy goats, chickens, hygiene products and other gifts for people in need, return for a 10th year at a record 145 sites, with nine countries including South Korea, Taiwan and Hungary hosting for the first time. Speaking at Tuesday's global launch, Elder Peter M. Johnson of the Seventy called Jesus Christ "the ultimate giver and the Prince of Peace" and encouraged people to bring friends and family to a machine nearby.


Sources:

  • Light the World turns 10 with a record number of Giving Machines - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: The world needs young adults now: 4 Latter-day Saint leaders’ pleas to young adults
item.description:
Four leaders of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints addressed young adults Sunday in Orem, Salt Lake City, Logan and Ogden, stressing faith in Christ, heeding prophets and serving others. Relief Society President Camille N. Johnson told the Salt Lake City group they needn't wait for school or career milestones to make a difference, saying "We need that kind of energy right now." After her devotional, Johnson joined hundreds of them making sleeping mats for homeless people; in Logan, Sister J. Anette Dennis helped assemble 3,400 humanitarian kits, while in Orem President Dieter F. Uchtdorf drew lessons from the Old Testament king Jehoshaphat and in Ogden Elder Clark G. Gilbert urged listeners to notice what a prophet repeats and pleads for.


Sources:

  • The world needs young adults now: 4 Latter-day Saint leaders’ pleas to young adults - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: How this single word can shape a life, according to Christian editor Anne Snyder
item.description:
Delivering BYU's Truman G. Madsen lecture on Tuesday, Comment magazine editor-in-chief Anne Snyder asked how the commitments people say yes to end up shaping who they become, borrowing Isaiah Berlin's contrast between foxes with many interests and hedgehogs who build around a single aim. Snyder, who identifies more with the fox, held up examples of committed lives, especially Swiss painter Manuel Dürr, picked to create a new set of 14 Stations of the Cross for St. Peter's Basilica, who came to accept that the meaning of his work was not his to determine. She closed by wishing students a commitment "substantial enough to shape a life but alive enough to keep listening."


Sources:

  • How this single word can shape a life, according to Christian editor Anne Snyder - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Mariya Manzhos

item.title: Episode 323: The transformative power of gratitude
item.description:
On the Church News podcast, BYU assistant psychology professor Jenae Nelson tells reporter Mary Richards what her new research found when it set thanks directed to God beside gratitude in general and followed each against well-being. The kind she means is not a "naive gratitude" blind to hardship, she says, but trust in God that holds even when life is hard.


Sources:

  • Episode 323: The transformative power of gratitude - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Church News

item.title: King Charles says Christian faith guides his reign
item.description:
Opening his first General Synod as king on Tuesday, Charles III said his Christian faith is "the compass which guides my every act as sovereign" and paid tribute to his late mother, Queen Elizabeth II, who presided over at least 10 openings of the Church of England's governing body. The king urged members to deepen ties with Catholic and Orthodox Christians, citing recent talks with Pope Leo and Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew, and to keep persecuted Christians in the Middle East and Holy Land in mind. He also asked them to debate in a spirit of unity and to "put yourself in the shoes of those with whom you disagree" when they differ.

item.title: Church of Jesus Christ advances 3 temples in Latin America
item.description:
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints broke ground Saturday, Nov. 14, on temples in Cuernavaca, Mexico, and Piura, Peru, and on Monday the First Presidency released a site map and location for the planned Rivera Uruguay Temple. Presiding in Cuernavaca, Mexico Area President Elder Moisés Villanueva called temples "places of peace" where people can draw closer to God and Christ, while Elder Steven C. Barlow blessed the Piura site, Peru's eighth announced temple. The single-story Mexico and Peru buildings are planned at about 19,000 and 18,800 square feet, and the 9,170-square-foot Rivera temple, near the Brazil border, will eventually be Uruguay's second operating temple.


Sources:

  • Church of Jesus Christ advances 3 temples in Latin America - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: How Church-owned camps, new and old, are strengthening youth
item.description:
A short Church News teaser, which sends readers to TheChurchNews.com for the full story, centers on Shipp Family Recreation Camp, a new Church-owned camp for young people described as Georgia's first. The excerpt says a Georgia stake that had staged a pioneer trek for its youth every four years for over two decades was left searching for a new site after a state park canceled its booking about 90 days before the June trek.


Sources:

  • How Church-owned camps, new and old, are strengthening youth - deseret.com

item.title: Elder Rasband visits Mia Love’s son on his mission
item.description:
Elder Ronald A. Rasband, an apostle, met with Elder Peyton Love, who is serving a mission in the Dominican Republic, to talk about missionary service and the legacy of Peyton Love's mother, former Utah Rep. Mia Love, who died of glioblastoma in March 2025. The families' ties run through missionary work: Rasband presided over the New York New York North Mission, and Peyton Love said his father, Jason Love, served under Rasband and trained the missionary who baptized Mia Love. Rasband, who recalled Mia Love asking him to bring his favorite Bible to her congressional swearing-in, told Peyton Love that "sometimes the veil is very thin" and that he would feel her presence.


Sources:

  • Elder Rasband visits Mia Love’s son on his mission - deseret.com

item.title: 10 years on the Conference Center stage: 1 performer’s ‘Luz de las Naciones’ story
item.description:
Amy Ortiz, who first stepped onto the Conference Center stage at 11 in the children's choir of Luz de las Naciones, looks back on performing a 10th year in the Church of Jesus Christ's Spanish-language celebration of Latin American music, dance and faith. Ortiz's family had emigrated from Mexico three years before joining the roughly 1,000-member cast in 2012, hoping the show would keep the children tied to their Mexican heritage, and Ortiz writes that it also bred a love for other cast members' homelands and made it possible to feel at home in both Mexico and the U.S. Recalling moments such as singing This Is the Christ in Spanish that first year, Ortiz credits the performances with strengthening a testimony of Jesus Christ, and Ortiz's mother calls the years of preparation "worth every sacrifice."


Sources:

  • 10 years on the Conference Center stage: 1 performer’s ‘Luz de las Naciones’ story - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: Latter-day Saint leader invites followers of Jesus Christ to become peacemakers in ‘hearts, homes and communities’
item.description:
President Dallin H. Oaks' Christmas message, shared Sunday in a YouTube video with his counselors in the First Presidency and included in the December 2026 Liahona, presents Jesus Christ as the Prince of Peace and invites believers to follow his example by making peace in their own lives, families and communities. Oaks described the joy surrounding Christ's birth as a reflection of the "ultimate joy and peace" offered through his Atonement. The article connects the invitation to Oaks' recent focus on peace, including a September National Cathedral address on the Constitution's role in compelling a divided people to work together and Nov. 8 social media posts calling Christ "the way to joy and peace."


Sources:

  • Latter-day Saint leader invites followers of Jesus Christ to become peacemakers in ‘hearts, homes and communities’ - deseret.com

item.title: A sports podcaster toured where young Latter-day Saint men and women prepare to serve missions. Here’s what he learned
item.description:
Drake Toll, host of the Locked on Big 12 podcast, who is not a Latter-day Saint and knew nothing of the Missionary Training Center until BYU athletics invited him, toured the Provo facility last month hours before BYU's 28-24 win over Notre Dame, alongside other media members, athletic director Brian Santiago and former Cougars quarterback Taysom Hill. In a 45-minute meeting, Toll asked missionaries bound for Thailand how they handle misconceptions and hate aimed at their church, and he said their top answer was "to love people, that love unlocks understanding". Weeks later, what stays with Toll is the sacrifice of 18- to 20-year-olds, among them a sister who paused BYU classes to serve and an elder who would know of a BYU win only by spotting fireworks over LaVell Edwards Stadium; being in that room, Toll said, meant getting "to look sacrifice in the eye and hear its voice".


Sources:

  • A sports podcaster toured where young Latter-day Saint men and women prepare to serve missions. Here’s what he learned - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Krysyan Edler
